subjects.displayTitle: Women’s roles: education, courage, and the common good
subjects.introduction: What possibilities open for a society when women can bring their knowledge, judgment, and courage fully into its life? These readings connect women’s advancement with the progress of humanity, moving between education, public speech, spiritual leadership, family life, and peace. Letters encourage particular women and gatherings; accounts of historical figures challenge assumptions about who can lead or teach. The importance assigned to mothers as first educators joins a wider summons to learning and service in every field. Some passages preserve the gendered idioms and social conditions of their time, inviting careful attention to how courage, dignity, and spiritual excellence are described. Neighboring subjects connect these responsibilities with equality, children’s education, cultural change, and prayer. Acts presents Priscilla and Aquila helping an eloquent teacher deepen his understanding. Their shared work offers a comparative starting point for considering whose insight a community recognizes and how it nurtures that insight.
subjects.arc: Begin with humanity’s shared progress, establish equality and education, follow women into teaching and public life, consider historical language and constraints, then return to courage, compassion, and enduring service.

Compare their shared teaching with this compilation’s accounts of women’s learning and spiritual leadership. What makes a community able to recognize insight across established expectations?

subjects.displayTitle: Equality of women and men: the flight of a shared humanity
subjects.introduction: A bird with one strong wing and one weak wing cannot rise, however hard it beats the air. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá returns to that image again and again, and it changes the question of equality from a matter of fairness between two parties into a matter of whether humanity as a whole can fly at all. Beneath the image lies a claim about human nature: women and men alike bear the divine image, and in the sight of God the only distinction between them is purity of heart and nobility of deed. From that root grow practical demands, for equal education, for rights and opportunity, for partnership in marriage rather than mastery, for women’s voice in the councils that decide between war and peace. The Qur’an’s verse naming women and men together in faith, patience, charity and remembrance [1] shows how old this pairing is in scripture. The journey continues toward the station and role of women in the new age, and toward the wider ordering of Bahá’í principles in which equality stands beside peace, education and the end of prejudice.
subjects.arc: Begin with interdependent progress, explore the spiritual basis of equality, follow education into rights and public participation, consider historical settings and institutional distinctions, and conclude with partnership and peace.

order.why: Open with the two wings and their shared flight.
Ground equality in the manifestation of divine names and attributes.
shortened: Know thou, O handmaid, that in the sight of Baha, women are accounted the same as men, and God hath created all humankind in His own image, and after His own likeness. That is, men and women alike are the revealers of His names and attributes, and from the spiritual viewpoint there is no difference between them. Whosoever draweth nearer to God, that one is the most favored, whether man or woman. How many a handmaid, ardent and devoted, hath, within the sheltering shade of Baha, proved superior to the men, and surpassed the famous of the earth.

order.why: Read the same effulgence shining upon women and men.
Connect rights and opportunity with the rejection of supposed innate deficiency.
shortened: It has been objected by some that woman is not equally capable with man and that she is deficient by creation. This is pure imagination. The difference in capability between man and woman is due entirely to opportunity and education.
The purpose, in brief, is this: that if woman be fully educated and granted her rights, she will attain the capacity for wonderful accomplishments and prove herself the equal of man.

order.why: Consider how limits imposed on women also limit men.
Read inequality as a source of discord.
Bring the principle into marriage as partnership.
Hear the removal of distinctions in the Supreme Pen’s language.
shortened: The Supreme Pen has removed the distinctions between servants and handmaidens, and through perfect grace and all-embracing mercy has established all upon a single plane.
In this Day the Hand of divine grace hath removed all distinctions. The servants of God and His handmaidens are regarded on the same plane.

order.why: Read equal respect beside differences of love and conduct.
Consider bounty embracing different circumstances and capacities.
Keep the concise affirmation of a common plane.
Read the related declaration of an equal station.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! The favours of the Kingdom are boundless and limitless, and they are beyond question and vain imagination. Therefore, male and female are one and the same, and men and bridal handmaidens enjoy an equal station. The one who advances more is nearer, and whoever is further enthused, is closer.

order.why: Hear the reported affirmation concerning the Kingdom.
Consider justice and equity without preference.
Read the radiance of faith across sex.
Explore divine image and likeness as a general human reality.
shortened: In the Torah it is written that God said, "Let us create man in Our image, after Our likeness," and in a tradition of the Prophet Muhammad it is stated: "God created Adam in His image." The meaning of this image is the divine image, that is, man reflects the attributes of God and manifests the qualities of the Lord.

Thus, man is a sign of the All-Merciful, created in the divine image and likeness. This applies generally and is not specific to men excluding women, for in God's sight there is no male and female. Whoever is more perfect is nearer to God, be it man or woman.

order.why: Keep the companion affirmation that all humanity bears the image.
Read knowledge, kindness, and purity as measures of nearness.
Consider good deeds and a pure heart in place of sex as a measure.
Read the source’s natural analogies alongside education and peace.
shortened: In the vegetable and animal kingdoms sex exists in perfect equality and without distinction or invidious estimate. The animal, although inferior to man in intelligence and reason, recognizes sex equality. Why should man, who is endowed with the sense of justice and sensibilities of conscience, be willing that one of the members of the human family should be rated and considered as subordinate?

In past ages humanity has been defective and inefficient because it has been incomplete. War and its ravages have blighted the world; the education of woman will be a mighty step toward its abolition and ending, for she will use her whole influence against war.

order.why: Consider the capacity to receive virtues and bestowals.
Read shared faculties and bounty within the human family.
Join faith with humanitarian action.
Question distinctions attributed to human choice rather than divine creation.
shortened: Another teaching is that there shall be perfect equality between men and women. Why should man create a distinction which God does not recognize?

order.why: Hear the concise appeal to common human origins.
Consider the source’s reversal of social loftiness and lowliness.
shortened: This is the Day whereon the distinctions of loftiness and lowliness have been abolished. Any soul, whether male or female, who hath turned unto the True One is reckoned as being of the True One, and apart from that is mentioned before the All-Merciful as being among the lost, even if they were of the most exalted in creation.

order.why: Read the ascendancy of spiritual qualities and the call to peace and fellowship.
Examine masculine and feminine terms as metaphor in this text.
shortened: O dust at the threshold of grandeur! Masculinity and femininity pertain to the soul, not to the body - to the heart, not to clay. For these two physical attributes are metaphorical, while their spiritual reality is truth. For we observe that a male person with an elephant-like physique can be as lowly, contemptible and weak as an ant, while behind the veil of chastity and purity, a female can be the epitome of strength and power - the former enslaved by self and passion, the latter noble through reason and restraint; the former sinful and the latter virtuous. Thus it becomes clear and evident that manliness and wisdom belong to the heart, not to water and clay.

order.why: Keep the source’s concise gendered idiom in that interpretive setting.
shortened: Today the handmaidens of God are accounted as men. Blessed are they and joy be unto them!

order.why: Read the companion statement without imposing a new meaning upon it.
Consider the contrast honoring steadfast handmaidens.
Read the crown image beside the common plane.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! In this precious age, the century of the mighty and omnipotent Lord, women have placed the crown of men upon their heads, inasmuch as all are gathered on the same plane.

order.why: Consider equality itself as a new garment and diadem.
shortened: O ye beloved maid-servants of God! In this most wonderful Dispensation God hath clothed the women with a new garment and hath crowned their heads with a glorious diadem - and that is equality between men and women.

order.why: Read the reported arguments about justice, faculties, and opportunity.
shortened: The other class, now representing the minority, but which ere long may become the majority, is of the opinion that perfect equality already exists. Those who are of this minority declare, first, that God is just, and justice demands an equal distribution of good gifts. They reason logically that it would be tyranny for God to show partiality, and the Lord is free from tyranny. They declare, secondly, that both man and woman being human all faculties and powers should be shared in common; that since creationally one sex has not been shown preference over the other we should not make a distinction that God has not created.

It must be admitted that in the past woman has not had the same educational opportunities that man has received, but when she is given equal advantages undoubtedly she will become his peer in knowledge and attainments.

order.why: Connect unequal opportunity with estimates of inferiority.
shortened: In proclaiming the oneness of mankind He taught that men and women are equal in the sight of God and that there is no distinction to be made between them. The only difference between them now is due to lack of education and training. If woman is given equal opportunity of education, distinction and estimate of inferiority will disappear. The world of humanity has two wings, as it were: One is the female; the other is the male. If one wing be defective, the strong perfect wing will not be capable of flight.

order.why: Read equal education and rights together.
Consider the equal obligation to educate girls and boys.
shortened: Girls are like boys - there is absolutely no difference. Ignorance in both is blameworthy, and lack of education in both types is repugnant. "Are those who know equal with those who know not?" This command is binding for both groups. In fact, if viewed with true insight, the education and training of girls is more necessary than boys, for these daughters will one day become mothers and nurturers of children.

order.why: Read a shared course of study as contributing to unity.
Join education with equal regard.
shortened: But the children of men are in need of education and civilization, and they require to be polished, till they become bright and shining. Man and woman both should be educated equally and equally regarded.

order.why: Keep the concise call for equal educational opportunity.
Read the same education and privileges as a brother.
Consider women’s education in relation to children’s spiritual development.
shortened: The education of women is more important than the education of men, because when women are educated, children also develop in spiritual life.

order.why: Keep the reported argument for prioritizing girls’ education.
Follow education toward occupations and accomplishment.
Read rights as enabling the acquisition of perfections.
Keep the natural analogies attributed while following its argument about opportunity.
shortened: Sex is not particularized to humanity; it exists throughout the animate kingdoms but without distinction or preference. In the vegetable kingdom there is complete equality between male and female of species. Likewise, in the animal plane equality exists; all are under the protection of God.

Woman's lack of progress and proficiency has been due to her need of equal education and opportunity. Had she been allowed this equality, there is no doubt she would be the counterpart of man in ability and capacity. The happiness of mankind will be realized when women and men coordinate and advance equally, for each is the complement and helpmeet of the other.

order.why: Distinguish equality affirmed as a principle from capacities becoming manifest in practice.
shortened: The realities of things have been revealed in this radiant century, and that which is true must come to the surface. Among these realities is the principle of the equality of man and woman -- equal rights and prerogatives in all things appertaining to humanity. Baha'u'llah declared this reality over fifty years ago. But while this principle of equality is true, it is likewise true that woman must prove her capacity and aptitude, must show forth the evidences of equality. She must become proficient in the arts and sciences and prove by her accomplishments that her abilities and powers have merely been latent.

order.why: Read the recognition that respected women still lacked fully realized rights.
shortened: In Europe and America, women are truly respected but their legitimate rights have not yet reached the degree of perfection, for their education in sciences and arts is not yet complete, and so forth from the divine teachings which are truly the life of the world and humanity today.

order.why: Consider the emphasis on acquiring sciences, virtues, and demonstrated capacities.
shortened: You must strive greatly, endeavor in acquiring sciences, exert effort in comprehending the realities of things, and devote boundless energy to human virtues. Know that divine grace encompasses you.

Women will progress when men themselves testify that women are equal to them. There is no need for struggle and contention. After children in school strive and acquire sciences and reach the utmost degree of perfection, everyone testifies that they are perfect - their very deeds testify to their perfection.

order.why: Read learning and argument as preparation for public contribution.
Consider women’s achievements as evidence of spiritual empowerment.
shortened: In this wondrous Dispensation, the favors of the Glorious Lord encompass the handmaidens of the All-Merciful, therefore they must, like men, snatch the ball from the field so it may be proven and established that the penetrating power of the Word of God in this new cycle has made women equal to men, and in the field of tests they seize the ball from the arena.

order.why: Read the particular recognition of women’s teaching work.
shortened: Most lovingly convey on behalf of `Abdu'l-Baha, the warmest Abha greetings to all the maidservants of God, and say that in this Dispensation, women have assumed the same position as men, nay rather in Europe and America they have even surpassed men in the teaching work as well as in their attraction to the Divine fragrances.

order.why: Keep the concise account of women teachers in America.
Read the companion description of lectures and reasoned proofs.
Consider the possibilities opened by women’s organized advancement.
shortened: Without doubt, women's groups are advancing in this age and striving to become equal with men. This is a great intention. If women's groups progress and gain power, they will accomplish many things they are currently unable to do.

order.why: Read the movement from seclusion into knowledge.
shortened: O handmaidens of the Court of Unity! The light of truth in this mighty Dispensation has cast its rays upon all, making no distinction between male and female. Women have attained the station of men, and those who were secluded have hastened to the arena of knowledge.

order.why: Consider recognition, certitude, and eloquence in the account of achievement.
Hear the promise of further entry into public activity.
shortened: O handmaid of God! Glad tidings! For in this divine Cycle women will soon gallop in the arena of men. In America, the clamor of the handmaids of the All-Merciful has shaken the very foundations. Behold what is happening!

order.why: Read endeavor as the ground of advancement.
shortened: O thou leaf who art well assured! In this divine Dispensation, and in this heavenly Age, mankind has become freed from the shackles of the distinction between the feminine and the masculine. The one who exerteth the utmost endeavor, is the one who advanceth and excelleth. How numerous are the men who remained behind [the veil], and how many the women who became the heroines of the field.

order.why: Keep the polo and heroism imagery focused on service.
shortened: Now, in this wondrous Revelation, women have indeed surpassed men, and this limitation hath been removed. All have been accounted with the same station. Whosoever ariseth further, shall obtain a greater share; and the valiant hero who urgeth ahead and hit the polo ball of service, will carry off the prize, and it maketh no difference whether man or woman, whether male or female. The Lord hath exalted the veiled woman above the men, she hath triumphed over the largest of armies, and hath won the leading prize in the fields of ecstasy and delight.

order.why: Consider the comparison with Rustam in its literary setting.
shortened: O pure leaf, throughout the dispensations men were the heroes of the battlefield and the valiant members of the army of revolt, but in this great cycle some women will arise who will become the envy of men, and the example to be emulated by the traditional hero, Rustam.

order.why: Read dignity through the metaphor of a new garment.
Keep the comparison with men in the West as a contextual statement.
shortened: In this cycle females have the station of males, rather in the West women have achieved superiority over men.

order.why: Read the particular assurance addressed to two women.
shortened: O ye two cherished handmaidens of the Abha Beauty! Although in ancient times the status of women was inferior compared to men, in this glorious Dispensation women are equal to men. Indeed, some of the handmaidens of the All-Merciful have outstripped men in the arena.

order.why: Distinguish circumstances in Persia from the reported equality of the Kingdom.
Read reported generalizations about gifts alongside its final measure of nearness to God.
Consider the reported shift from force toward love, service, and fuller balance.
shortened: The world in the past has been ruled by force, and man has dominated over woman by reason of his more forceful and aggressive qualities both of body and mind. But the balance is already shifting; force is losing its dominance, and mental alertness, intuition, and the spiritual qualities of love and service, in which woman is strong, are gaining ascendancy. Hence the new age will be an age less masculine and more permeated with the feminine ideals, or, to speak more exactly, will be an age in which the masculine and feminine elements of civilization will be more evenly balanced.

order.why: Read the full exchange, keeping the visitor’s answers distinct from the speaker’s words.
Retain the reporter’s question and the answer about rights and education.
shortened: Question: I have heard that you teach equality of rights between men and women.

Answer: The equality of rights between men and women is better established in America than elsewhere, and is advancing day by day. However, until complete equality between male and female is achieved in rights, the world of humanity will not make extraordinary progress. Women constitute one important pillar of two mighty pillars and are humanity's first teachers and educators, for mothers are the first teachers of young children. They establish moral character and educate children, who later study in higher schools. Now if the teacher and educator is deficient, how can the one educated become perfect? Therefore, the progress of women brings about the progress of men, hence women must be given complete education so they may reach the level of men.

order.why: Read the two wings in an address to the Women’s Freedom League.
shortened: Humanity is like a bird with its two wings -- the one is male, the other female. Unless both wings are strong and impelled by some common force, the bird cannot fly heavenwards. According to the spirit of this age, women must advance and fulfill their mission in all departments of life, becoming equal to men. They must be on the same level as men and enjoy equal rights. This is my earnest prayer and it is one of the fundamental principles of Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Consider equality as necessary to social and political progress.
shortened: And let it be known once more that until woman and man recognize and realize equality, social and political progress here or anywhere will not be possible. For the world of humanity consists of two parts or members: one is woman; the other is man. Until these two members are equal in strength, the oneness of humanity cannot be established, and the happiness and felicity of mankind will not be a reality.

order.why: Read women’s participation as essential to considering all sides of public questions.
shortened: In all questions which concern the welfare of a nation, is not the woman's view as important as the man's, if one would get a just and true consideration of all sides of that question? Therefore I am in favour of votes for women on every subject.

order.why: Keep the reported suffrage milestones in their historical setting.
Hear the expectation that equal rights will be realized.
Read the reported humorous reversal concerning which sex should demand equality.
Consider the two wings alongside the declaration of political detachment.
shortened: Regarding women's suffrage, this is a political issue and I am detached from all political matters, however I will say this much: both men and women are human and are like two wings for the world of humanity. If either of these wings is weak, the bird cannot fly. If both wings are strong, humanity will soar to the highest heaven.

order.why: Read the discussion of participation, voting, military exemption, and the House of Justice in full.
Keep the brief acknowledgment of exceptions.
Read the source’s categorical affirmation alongside its qualification.
shortened: Equality of men and women, except in some negligible instances, has been fully and categorically announced. Distinctions have been utterly removed.

order.why: Retain the related qualification in its own wording.
Read the reported question and answer on institutional membership as a distinct source.
Consider women’s membership in a meeting for the Temple.
Read a shared table as an enacted sign of equality.
shortened: In the olden time, it was not possible for women to sit at table in equality with the men, but in this Day it is different, and the change has been largely brought about by the position given to women in free America. It is the power of Baha'u'llah that made it possible for these American women to sit at this Table with these pilgrims. This is to show that in the Kingdom of Abha there will be equality established between women and men. They are equal.

order.why: Keep the account of meeting together across a former social barrier.
shortened: In the East it was prohibited for men and women to assemble in the same room. However in this Dispensation, the women have the same rank as men, and there is not the least difference between the two.

order.why: Read unity within the partnership of marriage.
Consider sympathy and friendship, retaining the report’s omissions.
Read the source’s connection between women’s influence and preventing war.
Connect equality with peace and the removal of prejudice.
Place equal rights within the teachings’ account of the world’s life.
shortened: Yet another of the teachings of Baha'u'llah is the equality of men and women and their equal sharing in all rights. And there are many similar principles. It hath now become evident that these teachings are the very life and soul of the world.

order.why: Read equality among a wider enumeration of principles.
Consider the connection with economic welfare and spiritual civilization.
Keep equality beside reason, peace, and the critique of prejudice.
Read the brief connection with economic principles.
shortened: They establish the equality of both sexes and propound economic principles which are for the happiness of individuals.

order.why: Join unity between women and men with equality of rights.
shortened: Seventh, unity between men and women and equality of rights.

order.why: Retain the concise enumeration.
shortened: Sixth is equality between men and women, and so forth.

order.why: Keep the separately reported enumeration in its source wording.
Return to the bird’s two wings and prosperity.
Read the brief companion image of strengthened wings.
Keep the interview’s formulation of the same relationship.
Read the reported question about access to life’s fullest opportunities.
Consider religion’s relationship to unequal privileges.
shortened: In the sight of the Heavenly Father all are equal. The religion of God is for the equalization of rights and not for the gradation of classes and the distribution of privileges. The religion of God is the leveller of all social inequalities and the destroyer of sacerdotal distinctions.

order.why: Keep the source’s comparative claim about earlier religions attributed to this address.
Read the report’s historical priority claim in its own setting.
Consider the reported response when the principle was proclaimed.
Read the historical account of denied education and public voice.
shortened: Women used to be oppressed in the Orient. They were in every respect humiliated. They were deprived of the opportunity to gain knowledge. They could not study science or art, and in politics they had no voice at all. Men did not consider them their equal. Baha'u'llah announced that women have the same right as men. He uplifted their conditions. He said, "The world of humanity has two wings, the one is man, the other woman."

order.why: Keep the broad account of former dispensations attributed to this report.
shortened: In all the former dispensations, men were considered superior to women. Women were lower than men; nay, rather during some of the past ages women were made captives of men. For example during the Mosaic dispensation women were captives of men, but in the dispensation of Baha'u'llah, His Bestowals have made men and women equal. He caused the people to put into active practice this social equality and declared that the women in this age shall make extraordinary advancement and they shall reach to such a degree, that no difference will be left between men and women.

subjects.displayTitle: Beyond party conflict: service, impartiality, and public responsibility
subjects.introduction: How can a community work for the good of society while remaining free of party rivalry? These readings approach that question through education, moral development, reconciliation, and service. Many letters respond to upheaval in Iran and the dangers facing a persecuted community; others address elections, public employment, spiritual assemblies, and cooperation with people pursuing shared aims. Their repeated calls to abstain from political interference sit beside explicit accounts of duties to the nation and government. Attention to circumstance, the meaning of service, and the distinction between public responsibility and factional allegiance is therefore essential. Neighboring subjects deepen the inquiry into government, the protection of the Faith, and relations between rulers and people. A passage from First Peter offers a distinct religious account of civic respect, good conduct, and freedom understood through service to God. The compilation invites reflection on how impartial goodwill becomes constructive action.
subjects.arc: Begin with constructive service and goodwill, distinguish public responsibility from factional allegiance, read the warnings in their historical settings, examine community practice, then consider later explanations and cooperation for shared aims.
